external_primary_sources.title: Self-hosted runners reference
observed_claims: GitHub routes to an online and idle self-hosted runner matching required runs-on labels/groups.
If no online and idle matching runner exists, the job remains queued until a runner comes online.
If an assigned runner does not pick up the job within 60 seconds, the job is re-queued.
A self-hosted job queued for more than 24 hours fails.

external_primary_sources.title: Using self-hosted runners in a workflow
observed_claims: Default self-hosted labels include self-hosted, OS and architecture labels.
Multiple runs-on labels are cumulative; a runner must satisfy all specified labels.

external_primary_sources.title: Monitoring and troubleshooting self-hosted runners
observed_claims: Runner states include Idle, Active and Offline.
Offline can mean host down, runner application stopped, or loss of GitHub connectivity.
The runner config script supports --check for required GitHub network services.
Runner diagnostic logs are stored below _diag and systemd service state can be inspected with journalctl.
Runner.Listener creates the message listener and starts listening to the queue.
The listener awaits GetNextMessageAsync before dispatching work to the worker process.
Acquire-job failures have explicit throttling/backoff logic.
